newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Wing Tiek to sell Manila steel firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Wing Tiek to sell Manila steel firm stake.

text.p: Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd is selling its 75 percent stake in the National Steel Corp (NSC), Wing Tiek's local partner said.
An official of Manila's Westmont Bank, Wing Tiek's partner, said the deal had been nearly finalised and the official announcement would be made later this week.
The official, who asked not to be named, said three Asian companies had vied to purchase the 75 percent stake.
Westmont Bank is a subsidiary of Westmont Industries Bhd, which is controlled by Joseph Chong, managing director of the Wing Tiek group.
NSC used to be a Philippine government owned company in which Wing Tiek bought 75 percent earlier this year.

The state-owned National Development Corporation still owns 25 percent in the steel company and the government wanted to sell 20 percent to any other buyer and retain five percent to be sold to small investors at a later date.
But a bidding in October failed to attract any buyers for the 20 percent stake and under the agreement signed earlier, Wing Tiek was required to buy it.
The Westmont official said Wing Tiek could not raise the additional 2.8 billion pesos needed to buy the 20 percent and therefore decided to pull out of the firm.
Wing Tiek had already paid 12.2 billion pesos for the 75 percent stake. Japan's Marubeni Corp was part of this deal but it was not clear what interest it held.
NSC accounts for more than 40 percent of the Philippines' steel output with an annual production capacity of 3.5 million tonnes. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418939 fax 8176267
